extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians working on Mochizuki's IUT (arithmetic geometry/number theory) and advanced readers of IUTch I–III
extracted.subtask_description: Understanding and applying the formal definitions, compatibility conditions, and functorial constructions of F-/D-/D'-prime-strips, log-links, log-theta-lattices, and associated log-shells in the IUT (Mochizuki) framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constant Prime-strips (Corollary 11.24 (1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Applying the constructions of Corollary 11.21 (1),(3) to the underlying (cid:1)-Hodge theatre produces collections (cid:9)cns(yF(...))t that determine an F-prime-strip for each t in LabCusp(...). Identification of collections (cid:9)cns(yF(...))0 and (cid:9)cns(yF(...))hF>l i is effected via the diagonal isomorphisms of Corollary 11.21 (3), yielding a natural F (cid:13)-prime-strip yF(cid:13) and a natural identification isomorphism with the data contained in the (cid:2)-Hodge theatre.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow constructions in Corollary 11.21 (1),(3); use the specified diag identification. The resulting F-prime-strip is 'constant' in the sense given and comes with a natural mod identification to the underlying Hodge theatre data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theta and Gaussian Prime-strips (Corollary 11.24 (2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Applying Corollary 11.21 (4),(5) to the underlying bridge and (cid:1)-Hodge theatre yields collections (cid:9)Fenv(...) and (cid:9)Fgau(...) and global realised Frobenioids yCenv, yCgau. For each v in V, localisation isomorphisms produce associated F (cid:13)-prime-strips yF(cid:13)env and yF(cid:13)gau, and the evaluation isomorphisms of Corollary 11.21 (4),(5) determine an evaluation isomorphism of F (cid:13)-prime-strips.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct Fenv and Fgau data per Corollary 11.21 (4),(5) and use localisation/evaluation isomorphisms to produce the F-prime-strips; record the natural identification isomorphisms between the F' structures and the originating Hodge-theatre data (see Defn.10.5(4)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Full poly-isomorphism / (..)-link and gau-link (Corollary 11.24 (3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Given eval maps and functoriality of the algorithm, one obtains full poly-isomorphisms (called (cid:2)(cid:2)(cid:22)-link and gau-link) between F-prime-strips and induced maps between IsomF(...) and IsomF(...)I(...)-spaces; the second map equals the composition of the first with the evaluation isomorphism and the functorially obtained isomorphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When producing links between Hodge theatres or prime-strips, record the induced maps at the IsomF level and check that the evaluation/composition identities hold; label the resulting full poly-isomorphism as the appropriate '-link' (gau or non-gau).

rubrics_metrics.name: Horizontally Coric F'-prime-strips (Corollary 11.24 (4))
rubrics_metrics.description: There are natural isomorphisms among the unit-portion prime-strips (yF'(cid:2)(cid:22) ... env ... gau etc.) and composites with the poly-isomorphism induced by the full poly-isomorphism of F(cid:13)I(...). These composites are preserved ('shared') under both the (cid:2)(cid:2)(cid:22)-link and the gau-link; the value-group portion, however, is not shared under these links. The full poly-isomorphism further induces full poly-isomorphisms of the associated D'-prime-strips, called the D-(cid:2)(cid:1)-link.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify the natural identifications among unit portions and track which parts (unit vs value group) are preserved across links; the D'-prime-strip poly-isomorphism is obtained by passing to the associated D'-structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Horizontally Coric Global Realised Frobenioids (Corollary 11.24 (5))
rubrics_metrics.description: The full poly-isomorphism of D'-prime-strips induces an isomorphism of triples (D(...); Prime(D(...))) between y- and z-objects, compatible with R_{>0}-orbits and with the 'Kum' poly-isomorphisms obtained by the functorial algorithm in Corollary 11.21 (2). The R_{>0}-orbits are defined by diagonal R_{>0}-action on the divisor monoids.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When checking compatibility, ensure the triple-level isomorphism respects the R_{>0}-orbits and the Kummer-induced poly-isomorphisms as stated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tautological log-link for v in Vnon (Defn.12.1 (1))
rubrics_metrics.description: For v in Vnon: from the perfection and Kummer isomorphism one constructs an ind-topological field structure on the perfection of the unit group, defines the p_v-adic logarithm on this ind-topological group, transports the structure, and obtains an isomorphism log_v. The resulting y_v-equivariant diagram log(yFv) is called the tautological log-link associated to yFv. Define IyFv (Frobenius-like holomorphic log-shell) as a certain subset related to the log-orbit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement the Kummer/perfection constructions (see Section 5.1 and Remark 3.19.2), define the p_v-adic logarithm and the log-link diagram, and record IyFv as the Frobenius-like holomorphic log-shell associated to the codomain of any log-link yFv → zFv.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tautological log-link for v in Varc (Defn.12.1 (2))
rubrics_metrics.description: For v in Varc: using the triple (yCv,yDv,y(cid:20)v) and Kummer structure one constructs a topological field structure and the Archimedean logarithm on the universal covering; this yields an isomorphism log_v and a co-holomorphicisation-compatible tautological log-link log(yFv). One also defines IyFv (Frobenius-like holomorphic log-shell) in the Archimedean setting via closed line segments invariant under certain multiplications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the Archimedean analogue of the non-Archimedean construction (Section 5.2); record the universal covering, the Kummer data, and the closed line segment/orbit defining IyFv.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collection log(yF) and global IyF (Defn.12.1 (3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Define log(yF) as the collection {log(yFv)}_{v in V} forgetting the field-structure (only additive/ind-topological modules remain). For v in Vnon, regard the resulting objects as Fv-prime-strips determined by these log objects. Define the tautological log-link yF → log(yF) and the (full) log-link composites yF log→ zF. Put IyF := product of IyFv; IyF is the Frobenius-like holomorphic log-shell associated to yF and regarded as an object associated to the codomain of any log-link yF → zF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When working globally, collect the local constructions and use product/formal-collection notation; IyF aggregates local log-shells and is used in statements about log-links between global F-prime-strips.

rubrics_metrics.name: Locality to F' components (Defn.12.1 (4))
rubrics_metrics.description: For v in Vnon (resp. Varc), the ind-topological modules log(yFv) and the closed subspace IyFv can be constructed only from the v-component yF'(cid:2)(cid:22)_v of the associated F'(cid:2)(cid:22)-prime-strip, via the (cid:2)(cid:22)-Kummer structure; equivalently, constructions use only the perfect units and are unaffected by quotienting by O((cid:22)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This indicates a locality principle: local log-shells/modules depend only on the v-component of the associated F'-prime-strip and the (cid:2)(cid:22)-Kummer data; check Steps 2 and 3 of the referenced Propositions for implementation details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Log-link induces (poly-)isomorphisms on D- and D'-prime-strips (Prop.12.2 (1))
rubrics_metrics.description: A log-link yF log→ zF induces (poly-)isomorphisms yD (poly)→ zD and yD' (poly)→ zD' of D-prime-strips and D'-prime-strips respectively. In particular, the induced (poly-)isomorphism maps cns(yD) (poly)→ cns(zD).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When verifying a log-link, check the induced maps on associated D- and D'-structures and the compatibility at the cns(...) level as in the proposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compatibility with log-volumes (Prop.12.2 (2))
rubrics_metrics.description: For v in Vnon (resp. Varc), the diagrams lognon (resp. logarc) are compatible with the natural p_v-adic log-volumes (resp. angular and radial log-volumes) on the respective log-objects in the sense of formula (5.1) (resp. (5.2)) of the referenced propositions; when descending via (cid:9)gp/(cid:9)(cid:22)^N, one regards the object as having 'weight N' and descends the metric accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the log-link preserves the relevant log-volume measures; check the precise formulae in Proposition 5.2 / 5.4 when implementing compatibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frobenius-like holomorphic log-shell inclusions (Prop.12.2 (3))
rubrics_metrics.description: For v in Vnon (resp. Varc), there are inclusions relating y(cid:5)v, log(yFv), Im(...), and IyFv expressing 'upper semi-compatibility' (cf. inclusions Upper Semi-Compat. (non-Arch)/(Arch) in Sections 5.1/5.2). These inclusions assert containment of certain log-objects and images in IyFv.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When confirming Frobenius-like holomorphic log-shell properties, check the listed inclusions and the respective sections for the precise upper semi-compatibility statements and the sets Ik, exp_k(Ik) referenced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mono-analytic log-shells and functorial construction (Prop.12.2 (4))
rubrics_metrics.description: For v in Vnon (resp. Varc), there is a functorial algorithm (w.r.t. the split monoid yD'_v) to construct an ind-topological module log(yD'_v) (resp. topological module) and a topological submodule IyD'_v (the etale-like mono-analytic log-shell) equipped with p_v-adic (resp. angular/radial) log-volumes. There are natural Kummer-induced isomorphisms ('Kum poly') relating log(yF'(...)) and log(yD'(...)) and compatibility with the relevant group actions and log-volumes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the functorial algorithm of Proposition 5.2 / 5.4 to produce the mono-analytic log-shells and check the Kummer-induced poly-isomorphisms and action compatibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Etale-like holomorphic vertically coric log-shells (Prop.12.2 (5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a D-prime-strip (cid:3)D with associated D'-prime-strip, and F((cid:3)D) the F-prime-strip determined by cns((cid:3)D), if yF = zF = F((cid:3)D) and the log-link is the full log-link, then a functorial algorithm constructs a collection of topological subspaces I_(cid:3)D := IyF which are called vertically coric etale-like holomorphic log-shells associated to (cid:3)D, along with a collection of isomorphisms cns((cid:3)D) → I_(cid:3)D'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This supplies a vertically coric log-shell construction in the special case yF=zF; implement via the D-prime-strip functorial algorithm and record the resulting I_D collection and isomorphisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kummer isomorphisms non-compatibility (Remark 12.2.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Kummer isomorphisms (cid:9)cns(yF) Kum→ (cid:9)cns(yD) and (cid:9)cns(zF) Kum→ (cid:9)cns(zD) are not compatible with the (poly-)isomorphism (cid:9)cns(yD) (poly)→ (cid:9)cns(zD) of Proposition 12.2 (1), with respect to the diagrams lognon and logarc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume Kummer isomorphisms commute with the poly-isomorphisms on cns(D)-level; explicitly check compatibility failures when composing these maps in arguments or diagrams.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frobenius-picture of log-links and vertical coricity (Remark 12.2.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: A chain of F-prime-strips indexed by Z with their full log-links (the Frobenius-picture of log-links) induces chains of full poly-isomorphisms of D- and D'-prime-strips. Identifying D-objects by these full poly-isomorphisms yields a diagram expressing vertical coricity of cns(D); this diagram is not commutative (cf. Remark 12.2.1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assembling infinite or indexed chains of log-links, track induced poly-isomorphisms and realize that the resulting vertical coricity diagram will generally fail to commute due to Kummer incompatibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constituent-wise construction to preserve f1-synchronisation (Defn.12.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given an isomorphism (cid:4) : yHT D-(...) → zHT D-(...), the poly-isomorphisms determined on D-prime-strips uniquely determine poly-isomorphisms log(yF>) → zF> etc., and hence a log-link from yHT(...) to zHT(...). The construction must be carried out constituent-isomorphism-wise (for a single isomorphism first) to maintain the crucial global f1-synchronisation in the (cid:1)-Hodge theatre; performing it only via the overall poly-isomorphism (not constituent-wise) would collapse the synchronisation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always build log-links by first handling single constituent isomorphisms and then assembling into poly-isomorphisms to preserve the global f1 synchronisation; see Lemma 10.10(2), Prop.10.33, Corollary 11.20(3), and IUTch references for the rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Log-theta-lattice (Defn.12.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: A log-theta-lattice is either of the specified two-dimensional arrays/diagrams of full log-links indexed by pairs (n,m) (non-Gaussian version and Gaussian version). The diagrams consist of full log arrows horizontally and vertically and include both (cid:2)(cid:2)(cid:22)- and gau-versions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When constructing or using a log-theta-lattice, distinguish Gaussian vs non-Gaussian diagrams; the lattice organizes full log-links across two integer parameters and is the structural setting for the subsequent bi-coric statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need only two adjacent columns (Remark 12.4.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: For the proof of the main theorem, only two adjacent columns of the final-update log-theta-lattice are needed; in analogy with p-adic Teichmüller theory this corresponds to 'lifting to modulo p^2'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In practical implementations directed at the main theorem, one may restrict attention to two adjacent columns (i.e., limited horizontal extent) of the lattice, reducing complexity to the needed 'mod p^2' lifting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertical Coricity of Gaussian log-theta-lattice (Thm.12.5 (1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Fixing initial Th-data, the vertical arrows of any Gaussian log-theta-lattice induce full poly-isomorphisms between the associated D-(cid:2)(cid:1)-Hodge theatres (for fixed n).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When verifying the vertical structure of a Gaussian log-theta-lattice, check that vertical arrows produce full poly-isomorphisms at the level of D-Hodge theatres, as required by the theorem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Horizontal Coricity of Gaussian log-theta-lattice (Thm.12.5 (2))
rubrics_metrics.description: For fixed m, the horizontal arrows of the Gaussian log-theta-lattice induce full poly-isomorphisms between the associated F'(cid:2)(cid:22)-prime-strips.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check horizontal arrows for inducing the claimed full poly-isomorphisms on F' prime-strips; this is the horizontal analogue of vertical coricity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bi-coric F'-prime-strips (Thm.12.5 (3))
rubrics_metrics.description: By identifying appropriate cns(...) collections via diag isomorphisms, one obtains F' prime-strips (F'(cid:2) and F'(cid:2)(cid:22) variants) associated to D-prime-strips in the lattice. The poly-isomorphisms from vertical and horizontal coricity induce poly-isomorphisms among these F' prime-strips for arbitrary index shifts, making the F'-prime-strips bi-coric (both horizontally and vertically). The statement notes that poly-isomorphism sets may differ in size due to non-scheme-theoretic automorphisms of absolute Galois groups of MLFs, and some poly-isomorphisms need not be full.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To establish bi-coricity, assemble the horizontal and vertical poly-isomorphisms, verify the Kummer compatibilities, and note possible non-fullness or size differences arising from non-scheme-theoretic automorphisms (see Section 3.5 and Remark 8.5.1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Bi-coric mono-analytic log-shells (Thm.12.5 (4))
rubrics_metrics.description: The poly-isomorphisms arising from the bi-coricity induce poly-isomorphisms between the collections of mono-analytic log-shells and their log-modules (In;mD', In0;m0D', IF'(...), etc.), i.e., the log-shell structures are transported poly-functorially across the lattice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When transporting log-shells across the lattice via bi-coric poly-isomorphisms, ensure the induced maps on the log-modules and I-collections are recorded and checked for poly-isomorphism compatibility.
